title: Ensure client authentication is required
description: Without requirepass or an ACL password on the default user, any client that can reach the port has full access. Compliant when requirepass is set or the default user is defined with a password (>pw / #hash) or is turned off. ACLs defined only in an aclfile must be reviewed separately. Checks /etc/redis/redis.conf (SKIP when it does not exist; RHEL uses /etc/redis.conf).
reference: CIS Redis Benchmark - Authentication / requirepass and ACL (verify section number for your release)

remediation.command: Set 'requirepass <long random secret>' (Redis < 6) or define ACL users with 'user <name> on ><secret> ~<keys> +@<categories>' and 'user default off' in redis.conf; restart and update clients

title: Ensure the default ACL user is not configured with nopass
description: 'user default ... nopass' explicitly allows password-less access with the default user's permissions. Checks /etc/redis/redis.conf (SKIP when it does not exist; RHEL uses /etc/redis.conf).
reference: CIS Redis Benchmark - Authentication / ACL default user (verify section number for your release)

remediation.command: Replace nopass with '><secret>' (or turn the user off with 'user default off') in redis.conf / the aclfile and restart, or ACL SETUSER default resetpass ><secret> followed by ACL SAVE

title: Ensure Redis binds only to specific interfaces
description: Without a bind directive, or with 0.0.0.0 / * / ::*, Redis listens on every interface. Compliant when a bind line exists and lists no wildcard address. Checks /etc/redis/redis.conf (SKIP when it does not exist; RHEL uses /etc/redis.conf).
reference: CIS Redis Benchmark - Network Security / Bind Address (verify section number for your release)

audit.command: f=/etc/redis/redis.conf; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1; awk '$1 == "bind" {b = 1; for (i = 2; i <= NF; i++) if ($i ~ /^-?(0\.0\.0\.0|\*|::|::\*|::0)$/) w = 1} END {print (b && !w) ? "compliant" : "noncompliant"}' "$f"

remediation.command: Set 'bind 127.0.0.1 -::1' plus only the private addresses clients use in redis.conf and restart Redis

title: Ensure protected-mode is enabled
description: protected-mode refuses external connections when no password is set.

title: Ensure the CONFIG command is renamed or blocked
description: CONFIG lets a client rewrite dir/dbfilename and write arbitrary files (a classic Redis-to-RCE path). Compliant when rename-command CONFIG is set or the default ACL user has -@dangerous / -@admin / -config. Checks /etc/redis/redis.conf (SKIP when it does not exist; RHEL uses /etc/redis.conf).
reference: CIS Redis Benchmark - Command Hardening / Dangerous Commands (verify section number for your release)

remediation.guidance: Add 'rename-command CONFIG ""' (or a secret name) to redis.conf, or restrict the default ACL user with -@dangerous, then restart Redis

title: Ensure redis.conf is not writable by group or readable by others
description: redis.conf contains requirepass and ACL secrets; restrict it to mode 640 or stricter. Checks /etc/redis/redis.conf (SKIP when it does not exist; RHEL uses /etc/redis.conf).
reference: CIS Redis Benchmark - File Permissions / Configuration File (verify section number for your release)

audit.command: p=$(stat -c %a /etc/redis/redis.conf 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if [ $((0$p & 037)) -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "mode $p"; fi

title: Ensure FLUSHALL and FLUSHDB are renamed or blocked
description: FLUSHALL/FLUSHDB destroy all data in one command. Compliant when rename-command FLUSHALL is set or the default ACL user has -@dangerous / -flushall. Checks /etc/redis/redis.conf (SKIP when it does not exist; RHEL uses /etc/redis.conf).
reference: CIS Redis Benchmark - Command Hardening / Dangerous Commands (verify section number for your release)

remediation.guidance: Add 'rename-command FLUSHALL ""' and 'rename-command FLUSHDB ""' to redis.conf (or use ACLs -@dangerous) and restart Redis

title: Ensure TLS is enabled
description: tls-port (Redis 6+) with tls-cert-file/tls-key-file encrypts client traffic; also set 'port 0' to disable the plain-text listener. Checks /etc/redis/redis.conf (SKIP when it does not exist; RHEL uses /etc/redis.conf).
reference: CIS Redis Benchmark - Network Security / TLS (verify section number for your release)

remediation.command: Set tls-port 6379, tls-cert-file, tls-key-file, tls-ca-cert-file and port 0 in redis.conf, restart Redis and configure clients for TLS
